summary: Recorded the sweep and extended the trim probe. The sweep execution (CheckRun 398a42387e1742c3b3f7cbfbbc0b75d4, exit 0, all seven cases) evaluated every comparison completely: the no-partition control at 2 ms holds, the partition at 2 ms and 4 ms holds (documented `Superseded` arm), and the partition at 8, 16, 40 and 80 ms is violated with valid witnesses — each resolving `ok` with assigned index 1 while the decided entry there was the new leader's entry and the caller's entry was in no decided log. So the false completion is the ordinary outcome once the tick period exceeds the re-synchronisation round trip, and the crate's own default tick period is 10 ms; I appended that account on the self-contained receipt, promoted the band to knowledge, and replaced the old two-point limitation. For the trim defect I extended the probe with the generalised trigger (ids {2,3,4} with a different leader and id 1 absent, plus the two-node {1,3}) and validated locally that both keep the compacted index at 0 with `trim(None)` returning ok and `trim(Some(1))` returning `NotAllDecided(0)`, so the trigger is now measured as 'largest node id exceeds the node count' rather than derived from the sizing code; that extended probe is submitted as the successor execution. Incomplete: that receipt is pending; the follower-origin variant of the runtime defect and the snapshot-then-trim variant remain unmeasured variants of the same causes.
